sources.entry: Roundup Issue Tracker - Simple-to-use and -install issue tracking system with command-line, web, REST, XML-RPC, and e-mail interfaces. Designed with flexibility in mind - not just another bug tracker. (Source Code) MIT/ZPL-2.0 Python/Docker

summary.name: Roundup Issue Tracker
summary.one_liner: Roundup is an issue tracking system whose source code page explains how to get the Mercurial repository, the GitHub mirror, and how to run the demo and tests.
use_cases: run the bundled Roundup demo locally
summary.what_it_does: The page is a code access page for the Roundup project. It gives Mercurial commands for read-only cloning from SourceForge and for read/write access over SSH, with write access requiring developer status. It also points to a GitHub mirror that lags the main repository by about a couple of weeks and is used for CI, with issues and pull requests not handled there. It explains that the demo runs with python demo.py at localhost port 8917 and that tests run with python -m pytest test. Project history is kept in CHANGES.txt.
notable: Mercurial repository hosted on SourceForge with a GitHub mirror used for CI
Runs out of the box with no dependencies, with a built-in demo on port 8917
Interfaces listed as command-line, web, REST, XML-RPC, and e-mail
Licensed MIT/ZPL-2.0 per the awesome-selfhosted listing
caveats: GitHub mirror lags the main Mercurial repository by a couple of weeks
Write access requires a SourceForge SSH login and being added as a Roundup developer
GitHub Issues and pull requests are not used; use issues.roundup-tracker.org instead
